title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and understand directions, take a bus, train or auto-rickshaw, and give instructions politely or informally.
intro: Odia towns are organised around **ଛକ** (*chhôkô*) — junctions or squares that serve as landmarks (Master Canteen Chhak, Rasulgarh Chhak…). In this unit you learn the three levels of **command** (formal, familiar, intimate) and the endings for movement: **-କୁ** 'to', **-ରୁ** 'from'.

vocab.en: to get on, board; to climb

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
phrases.note: ଶୁଣନ୍ତୁ 'listen' is the polite way to get attention.

phrases.en: How far is it from here?

phrases.native: ବେଶି ଦୂର ନୁହେଁ, ପାଞ୍ଚ ମିନିଟ୍ ବାଟ।
phrases.roman: besi durô nuheṃ, pañchô miniṭ baṭô.

phrases.en: Does this bus go to Puri?
Will you go to Lingaraj Temple? (to a driver)
How much will the fare be?
Where can I get a ticket?

grammar.title: Commands at three levels
grammar.body:
The imperative matches the three levels of 'you':

**Formal (ଆପଣ)**: stem + **-ଅନ୍ତୁ** — କରନ୍ତୁ, ଯାଆନ୍ତୁ, ଆସନ୍ତୁ, ବସନ୍ତୁ, ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ, ନିଅନ୍ତୁ, କୁହନ୍ତୁ, ରୁହନ୍ତୁ
**Familiar (ତୁମେ)**: stem + **-ଅ** — କର, ଯାଅ, ଆସ, ବସ, ଦିଅ, ନିଅ, କୁହ, ରୁହ
**Intimate (ତୁ)**: bare stem — କର୍, ଯା, ଆ, ବସ୍, ଦେ, ନେ, କହ, ରହ

To say **don't**, add ନାହିଁ (ଡେରି କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ) or, more gently, use the future + ନାହିଁ (ଡେରି କରିବେ ନାହିଁ). A polite request can also be a future question: ଏଠି ରଖିବେ? 'Will you stop here?'. With strangers like drivers and shopkeepers, formal forms are safest, though many people use ତୁମେ with drivers younger than them.

grammar.title: Movement: -କୁ (to), -ରୁ (from), -ରେ (by), ଯାଏ (up to)
grammar.body:
**-କୁ** marks the destination: ମନ୍ଦିରକୁ 'to the temple'. With ଯିବା and place names, -କୁ is often dropped: କଟକ ଯିବି 'I'll go to Cuttack'.
**-ରୁ** marks the starting point: ଷ୍ଟେସନରୁ 'from the station', ଏଠାରୁ 'from here'.
**-ରେ** also means 'by (vehicle)': ବସରେ 'by bus', ଟ୍ରେନରେ 'by train'.
**ଯାଏ** or **ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** after a noun means 'up to, as far as': ଛକ ଯାଏ.

A useful pattern for directions is the **-ଇ** participle ('having done'): ସିଧା **ଯାଇ** ବାଁକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ 'go straight and (then) turn left'.

examples.en: He/She is coming from the station.
Walk as far as the junction.
How far is the market from here?

dialogue.title: To the Lingaraj Temple
dialogue.setting: Sam asks a passer-by the way, then bargains with an auto-rickshaw driver in Old Town, Bhubaneswar.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Excuse me, where is the Lingaraj Temple?

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: ଏଠାରୁ ଟିକେ ଦୂର। ସିଧା ଯାଇ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଛକରୁ ବାଁ ପଟକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: eṭharu ṭike durô. sidha jai dwitiyô chhôkôru baṃ pôṭôku bulôntu.
lines.en: It's a bit far from here. Go straight and turn left at the second junction.

lines.speaker: Passer-by
lines.native: ହଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ କୋଡ଼ିଏ ମିନିଟ୍ ଲାଗିବ। ଅଟୋରେ ଯାଆନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: hôṃ, kintu koṛie miniṭ lagibô. ôṭore jaôntu.
lines.en: Yes, but it'll take twenty minutes. Take an auto.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Brother, will you go to Lingaraj Temple?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Fine. Drop me in front of the temple, please.

culture: Directions in Odisha are given by landmarks — a *chhak*, a temple, a well-known shop — rather than street names. Agree on the fare before getting into an auto-rickshaw, or use app-based autos in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. Address drivers and strangers as **ଭାଇ** (brother), **ଭାଇନା** or **ଅପା**. Note that non-Hindus are not allowed inside the Jagannath Temple in Puri or the Lingaraj Temple, though both can be viewed from outside.

tip.title: Asking where something is
tip.body:
- Get attention politely with **ଶୁଣନ୍ତୁ** 'excuse me' (lit. 'listen'), or call people **ଭାଇ** (brother) / **ଅପା** (sister).
- Then: place + **କେଉଁଠି?** — ବଜାର କେଉଁଠି? 'where's the market?'
- 'Near …' is **… ନିକଟରେ** or **… ପାଖରେ**: ଷ୍ଟେସନ ନିକଟରେ.

sentences.en: Excuse me, where's the market?

sentences.native: ଭାଇ, ଏଠି ନିକଟରେ ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ ଅଛି କି?
sentences.roman: bhai, eṭhi nikôṭôre byaṅkô ôchhi ki?
sentences.en: Brother, is there a bank near here?

sentences.native: ହଁ, ମନ୍ଦିର ପାଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: hôṃ, môndirô pakhôre goṭie byaṅkô ôchhi.
sentences.en: Yes, there's a bank next to the temple.

sentences.native: ଷ୍ଟେସନ ନିକଟରେ ଭଲ ହୋଟେଲ ଅଛି କି?
sentences.roman: sṭesônô nikôṭôre bhôlô hoṭelô ôchhi ki?
sentences.en: Is there a good hotel near the station?
Excuse me (sister), where's the pharmacy?
There's a big temple at the junction.
The hotel is in front of the station.
My shop is inside the market.
The temple is near our house.

lessons.title: Near or far?

tip.title: To, from, as far as: -କୁ, -ରୁ, ଯାଏ
tip.body:
- **-କୁ** = to: ବଜାରକୁ 'to the market'. With ଯିବା and place names it's often dropped: ପୁରୀ ଯିବି.
- **-ରୁ** = from: ମନ୍ଦିରରୁ 'from the temple', **ଏଠାରୁ** 'from here'.
- **ଯାଏ** after a noun = as far as: ଛକ ଯାଏ.
- Distance: place + ଏଠାରୁ କେତେ ଦୂର?

new: ବେଶି ଦୂର ନୁହେଁ, ପାଞ୍ଚ ମିନିଟ୍ ବାଟ।

sentences.en: How far is the station from here?
My village is very far from here.
I'm going to the market.
She is coming from the temple.
Does this road go to the station?
We're coming from the village.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଘର ଏଠାରୁ ଦଶ ମିନିଟ୍ ବାଟ।
sentences.roman: mo ghôrô eṭharu dôsô miniṭ baṭô.
sentences.en: My house is ten minutes from here.
It's a straight road as far as the junction.
The station isn't far.
This road is very long.

tip.title: Telling someone where to go
tip.body:
- To a stranger (ଆପଣ): stem + **-ଅନ୍ତୁ** — ଯାଆନ୍ତୁ 'go', ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ 'turn', କୁହନ୍ତୁ 'say'.
- To a friend (ତୁମେ): stem + **-ଅ** — ଯାଅ, ବୁଲ, ଚାଲ.
- Directions: **ଡାହାଣ ପଟକୁ** to the right, **ବାଁ ପଟକୁ** to the left, **ସିଧା** straight.

sentences.native: ସିଧା ଯାଆନ୍ତୁ, ତା'ପରେ ଡାହାଣ ପଟକୁ ବୁଲନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: sidha jaôntu, tapôre ḍahaṇô pôṭôku bulôntu.
sentences.en: Go straight, then turn right.
Go left at the junction.
Turn right at the first corner.

sentences.native: ସିଧା ଚାଲ, ମନ୍ଦିର ଡାହାଣ ପଟରେ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: sidha chalô, môndirô ḍahaṇô pôṭôre ôchhi.
sentences.en: Walk straight on — the temple is on the right. (to a friend)
Turn left, brother. (familiar)
Go straight as far as the corner. (to a friend)
Not right — turn left.
Please say that once more.
The bank is on the left, next to the shop.

tip.title: By bus, at the station: -ରେ
tip.body:
- **-ରେ** after a vehicle = by: **ବସରେ** 'by bus', **ଟ୍ରେନରେ** 'by train', ଗାଡ଼ିରେ 'by car'.
- The same **-ରେ** = at / in a place: ଷ୍ଟେସନରେ 'at the station'.
- Getting on and off: ବସରେ **ଚଢ଼ନ୍ତୁ** · ଷ୍ଟେସନରେ **ଓହ୍ଲାନ୍ତୁ**.
- Don't mix it up with -ରୁ 'from' and -କୁ 'to'.

sentences.en: I go to the office by bus.
We're going to Puri by train.
How long does it take to the airport by car?
Get on this bus.
Get off at the next station.
Is there a bus from the airport to the hotel?
You can get tickets at the station.
How much is a train ticket?
Does this train go to Cuttack?
The next bus is at ten.

tip.title: Asking a driver politely
tip.body:
- A future question is a polite request: ଷ୍ଟେସନ **ଯିବେ?** 'will you go to the station?', ଏଠି **ରଖିବେ?** 'will you stop here?'
- Or the polite command: **ଅଟକନ୍ତୁ** 'stop', **ରଖନ୍ତୁ** 'drop me'.
- 'Don't' = command + **ନାହିଁ**: ଅଟକନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ.
- Agree the **ଭଡ଼ା** before you get in.

sentences.en: Brother, will you go to the station?
Please stop in front of the bank.
Don't stop here — keep going straight.
Could you drop me near the junction?
Please go slowly.
Stop a moment, I'll get off.
What's the fare to the airport?
Come on, let's go by auto.
Eighty rupees is too much.
